editorial.marketOverview: The Nasdaq three-day outlook shifts from bearish to cautiously bullish following Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang and a reported extraordinary US cash-market rally. FT reports Nvidia +30%, Nasdaq 100 +7%, S&P 500 +4.9% intraday. The rebound is reported cash trading, not merely futures, but closing confirmation remains absent.
editorial.whatChanged: Huang's return reverses a critical leadership uncertainty and triggers a major reported stock and index response. Reuters flash composite PMI slowed to 54.6 from 55.9 but remained expansionary. The Open Watch feed updated at 13:57 UTC; Huang's return was independently reported rather than present in inspected leading curated events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The positive leadership catalyst and observed cash response justify upgrading the tactical bias. Still, the large rebound after Friday's liquidation may involve short covering. Synchronized breadth, volatility and SOX relative strength are unavailable, limiting confidence.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday is a volatile event-driven recovery attempt. Tuesday tests follow-through through consumer confidence and Dell earnings. Wednesday brings the major PCE/GDP/Beige Book stress test. A fragile bullish rebound replaces the prior bearish continuation base case.
editorial.bullCase: Restored leadership continuity draws buyers back to AI chips. Holding Monday's gains into Tuesday with improving breadth, falling VXN/VIX and stable yields would support a durable recovery.
editorial.bearCase: An outsized opening rally may fade as covering exhausts. Nvidia investigations, China customer concerns, high yields and inflation risks remain. A hot PCE or disappointing earnings could renew selling.
editorial.watchNext: Verify QQQ/SOX/SMH cash closes, breadth, VXN/VIX, correctly scaled matched 10Y/2Y, primary FedWatch and oil contract quotes. Watch HPE Monday, consumer confidence and Dell Tuesday, PCE/GDP Wednesday; separate catalyst forecasts from observed reactions.
